368078.title: The normality conjecture for the limiting rational-base word
368078.statement:
For each $k\geq 1$, let $\langle\operatorname{sat}(k)\rangle$ be the associated word, and define the infinite word

$$
\langle\operatorname{sat}(\infty)\rangle=\lim_{k\to\infty}\langle\operatorname{sat}(k)\rangle.
$$

An infinite word over a finite alphabet is **normal** if every word of length $\ell$ over that alphabet occurs with limiting frequency $1/b^\ell$, where $b$ is the alphabet size. **The normality conjecture.** The word $\langle\operatorname{sat}(\infty)\rangle$ is normal. This is stated as a stronger conjecture motivated by numerical evidence; its status is open.

368244.title: Axisymmetry conjecture for magnetic ground-state minimizers
368244.statement: Let $B\geq 0$ be the strength of a constant magnetic field, and let $\Omega^*(B)$ be a domain minimizing the first eigenvalue among the admissible domains of fixed volume. The magnetic field points along the $z$-axis. **Axisymmetry conjecture.** For any $B\geq 0$, the minimizer $\Omega^*(B)$ is axisymmetric with respect to the $z$-axis. This is suggested by numerical optimization, including computations without an imposed symmetry assumption; whether all minimizers have this symmetry remains open.

368305.title: Bensmail–Mc Inerney's vertex-capturing game conjecture
368305.statement:
For the vertex-capturing game $\operatorname{VC}(n)$ on the complete graph $K_n$, let $s_{\operatorname{VC}}(n)$ denote the optimal score difference between the two players.

**Bensmail–Mc Inerney's conjecture.**

$$
s_{\operatorname{VC}}(n)=\begin{cases} 2 & \text{if } n=2\\ 1 & \text{if } n\equiv 3 \pmod 4\\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}
$$

The source attributes this conjecture to Bensmail and Mc Inerney and states that it was confirmed for $n\leq 6$; its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.

368317.title: NP-completeness of mutual-visibility coloring
368317.statement:
A graph $G$ has a **mutual-visibility coloring** if its vertices can be colored so that the required mutual-visibility condition holds; the associated decision problem asks whether $G$ admits such a coloring with a prescribed number of colors.

**Mutual-visibility coloring conjecture.** The mutual-visibility coloring decision problem is NP-complete.

The paper proves NP-completeness for the independent version, even for graphs with universal vertices, and conjectures that the same computational complexity holds for the basic version.

368352.title: Degree-sequence and structural invariants conjecture for chromatic symmetric functions of unicyclic graphs
368352.statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be connected unicyclic graphs, where either each has a 3-cycle and an odd number of vertices, or each has a $c$-cycle for some $c\geq4$. Let $\mathbf{X}_G$ denote the chromatic symmetric function of a graph $G$. **Unicyclic graph invariants conjecture.** If

$$
\mathbf{X}_{G_1}=\mathbf{X}_{G_2},
$$

then $G_1$ and $G_2$ have the same degree sequence, the same number of non-trivial rooted trees, and the same number of internal edges. The conjecture concerns which structural features of connected unicyclic graphs are determined by their chromatic symmetric functions; it had been verified for graphs with $n\leq16$ vertices in the source, while the contrasting 3-cycle examples with an even number of vertices show why the parity restriction is necessary.

368397.title: Zheng–Sun's revised generalized Kriesell conjecture for non-regular graphs
368397.statement: Let $t>0$. A graph is **non-regular** if its vertex degrees are not all equal, and a **minimally $t$-tough graph** is a $t$-tough graph whose toughness decreases after deleting any edge. **Zheng–Sun's revised conjecture.** Every non-regular minimally $t$-tough graph has a vertex of degree $\lceil 2t\rceil$. The paper states that this revised conjecture fails for small graphs, since one of the counterexamples to the generalized conjecture is non-regular.

368742.title: Strong positive square-energy conjecture for graphs with many edges
368742.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$ and size $m$. **Strong positive square-energy conjecture.** If $m\ge n+1$, then

$$
s^+(G)\ge n.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the positive-energy side of the preceding conjecture for graphs having at least two more edges than vertices. It was proposed after computational investigation; the source reports checks of the conjectures for graphs up to $9$ vertices, but no general proof is given.

368743.title: Unicyclic graph square-energy conjecture
368743.statement:
Let $G$ be a unicyclic graph of order $n$, and let $k$ be the odd length of its unique cycle. **Unicyclic graph square-energy conjecture.**

$$
\begin{cases}
s^+(G)>n>s^-(G),&k\equiv3\pmod 4,\\
s^+(G)<n<s^-(G),&k\equiv1\pmod 4.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture is motivated by an exact calculation for cycles and further computational investigation. The source identifies unicyclic graphs as among the hardest cases for the main square-energy conjecture; no general proof is supplied.

368745.title: Positive square-energy bounds for maximal planar and outerplanar graphs
368745.statement:
A graph is **maximal planar** if it is planar and no edge can be added while preserving planarity, and **maximal outerplanar** if it is outerplanar and no edge can be added while preserving outerplanarity. **Maximal planar and outerplanar square-energy conjecture.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{If $G$ is maximal planar of order $n\ge10$, then }s^+(G)\ge3n;\\
&\text{if $G$ is maximal outerplanar of order $n\ge8$, then }s^+(G)\ge2n.
\end{aligned}
$$

These bounds are proposed as more accessible refinements of previously discussed questions for maximal planar graphs. They are motivated by computational investigation and super-additivity of square energy; the source gives no general proof.

368967.title: The 3-sum formula for Speyer's invariant
368967.statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be two $3$-connected graphs, each with a triangle $T_i\subset G_i$, and let $G_1\oplus_3G_2$ be a corresponding 3-sum. Define

$$
p_i=\left|\pi_0\left(G_i\setminus V(T_i)\right)\right|
$$

to be the number of connected components remaining after deleting the triangle vertices.

**3-sum conjecture.** The invariant satisfies

$$
\mathsf{N}_2(G_1\oplus_3G_2)=\mathsf{N}_2(G_1)+\mathsf{N}_2(G_2)-p_1p_2.
$$

The formula would reduce computations of $\mathsf{N}_2$ to highly connected graphs and includes a star--triangle relation as a special case. The paper reports computational confirmation but no proof.

368970.title: The 4-edge-twist congruence for Speyer's polynomial
368970.statement:
A **4-edge twist** of a graph $G_1$ is obtained from a minimal $4$-edge cut by reconnecting the four cut edges according to a double transposition. Let $G_2$ be any 4-edge twist of $G_1$.

**4-edge-twist conjecture.** Then

$$
g_{G_1}(t)\equiv g_{G_2}(t)\pmod{t^3\mathbb{Z}[t]}.
$$

Thus a 4-edge twist would preserve the first two nonzero coefficients of Speyer's polynomial. The paper presents this as a computationally supported relation and leaves it open.

368973.title: The complete bipartite and 4-partite Speyer polynomial formulas
368973.statement:
For $n\geq3$, let $K_{3,n}=\overline{K}_3\vee\overline{K}_n$ and $K_{1,1,1,n}\cong K_3\vee\overline{K}_n$.

**Complete multipartite formula conjecture.** Their Speyer polynomials are

$$
g_{K_{3,n}}(t)=t(nt^2+nt+t+2)(2+t)^{n-1}-3t(1+t)^{n+1}
$$

and

$$
g_{K_{1,1,1,n}}(t)=t(nt^2+nt+t+2)(2+t)^{n-1}.
$$

These formulas imply the quadratic growth $\mathsf{N}_2(K_{3,n})=\mathsf{N}_2(K_{1,1,1,n})=-n(n-3)/2$ and are supported by the computations in the paper.

369280.title: The conjectured quadratic eigenvector for the position matrix
369280.statement:
Let $M$ be the position matrix of the one-shelf shuffling machine, with entries $M_{ij}=p_{i,j}$, where $p_{i,j}$ is the probability that the card initially in position $i$ ends in position $j$. For $n\geq 3$, define a vector $\vec{v}$ by

$$
v_k=n^2-3nk+\frac{3k(k+1)}{2}-1.
$$

**The quadratic eigenvector conjecture.** $M$ has an eigenvalue-eigenvector pair $(\frac{1}{4},\vec{v})$ with multiplicity at least $1$. Numerical computation suggests this eigenvector formula; the conjecture concerns the spectrum of the position matrix and remains unproved in the supplied text.

369281.title: The conjectured nonzero spectrum of the position matrix
369281.statement:
Let $M$ be the position matrix of the one-shelf shuffling machine. Its eigenvalues describe the associated Markov chain on card positions; the previously established eigenvalues include $1$ and $0$ with the stated multiplicities. **The nonzero-spectrum conjecture.** The nonzero eigenvalues of $M$ are

$$
\frac{1}{2^{2i}},\qquad i=0,1,\ldots,\left\lceil\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

Numerical evidence is said to strongly suggest this form, but no proof or resolution is supplied in the text.

369568.title: Super Catalan number recurrence from generalized action graph path counts
369568.statement:
Let $G_n$ be the action graph associated with $S(0,n)$, and let $K_{\ell,v,n}$ be the number of paths of length $\ell$ in $G_n$ that start at a vertex labeled $v$ and end at a vertex labeled $n$. **Super Catalan computation conjecture.** The subsequent super Catalan number can be computed from the $n$-table of its previous action graph via

$$
S(0,n+1) = \displaystyle \sum_{\ell=0}^{n} \left(\frac{2}{2^\ell} \sum_{v=0}^{n} K_{\ell,v,n}\right).
$$

If the path-count recurrence conjecture holds, the authors believe this formula computes $S(0,n+1)$ from the $n$-table and establishes that $G_n$ satisfies Axiom1. The formula is presented as part of an approach whose general validity remains open.

369616.title: The line-graph inertia conjecture
369616.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $L(G)$ denote its line graph. Let $n^+(L(G))$ and $n^-(L(G))$ be the numbers of positive and negative eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $L(G)$, and let $s(L(G))$ be its signature. **Line-graph inertia conjecture.**

$$
n^+(L(G))\leq n^-(L(G))+1.
$$

Equivalently, $s(L(G))\leq 1$. The paper proves a weaker upper bound for line graphs and presents computational evidence for this sharper conjecture, which remains open.

369640.title: The intersection-number-zero criterion for plabic graphs
369640.statement: Fix a positive integer $m$, and let $G$ be a plabic graph of type $(k,n)$ with $\dim\Pi_G=km$. Let $T_G$ denote the associated family of $k$-planes. **Intersection-number-zero criterion conjecture.** The following are equivalent: (i) $\Pi_G$ has $m$-intersection number $0$; (ii) there is a plabic graph $G'$ of type $(k',n')$ with $1\leq k'<k$ and $\dim\Pi_{G'}<k'm$ such that every $V\in T_G$ contains some $V'\in\Pi_{G'}$; (iii) a graph move-equivalent to $G$ has a subgraph $G'$ and perfect orientation satisfying the assumptions of the sufficient criterion in Proposition 1. The equivalence is conjectural, based on computations for $m\leq 8$.

369642.title: Prime characterization conjecture for the reduced Dressian of the cyclic matroid
369642.statement:
Let $n\geqslant 7$ be an integer, and let ${\mathcal T}_n$ denote the cyclic matroid used in the paper. Write $\operatorname{\underline{Dr}}_{{\mathcal T}_n}$ for its reduced Dressian. **Reduced Dressian conjecture.**

1. The reduced Dressian $\operatorname{\underline{Dr}}_{{\mathcal T}_n}$ is one-dimensional if and only if $n$ is prime.
2. If $n=p$ is prime, then the one-dimensional fan $\operatorname{\underline{Dr}}_{{\mathcal T}_p}$ consists of exactly $\frac{p-1}{2}$ rays.

The conjecture concerns the combinatorial structure of the reduced Dressians of the cyclic matroids ${\mathcal T}_n$; the paper presents it after computations for several examples, and no resolution is supplied here.

369839.title: Stieltjes moment conjecture for vincular pattern Classes 1 and 2
369839.statement:
For each $n\geq 0$, let $P_n^{(1)}(x)$ and $P_n^{(2)}(x)$ be the generating polynomials for the number of occurrences of vincular patterns in Class $1$ and Class $2$, respectively. A sequence of polynomials is a **Stieltjes moment sequence** when it is represented by moments of a nonnegative measure.

**Stieltjes moment conjecture.** The sequences of polynomials

$$
\left(P_n^{(1)}(x)\right)_{n\geq 0},\qquad \left(P_n^{(2)}(x)\right)_{n\geq 0}
$$

are both Stieltjes moment sequences for $x\geq 0$.

The conjecture extends known positivity results for Class $3$, whose generating function has a Stieltjes-type continued fraction. The authors checked finitely many S-fraction coefficients for Classes $1$ and $2$, finding them nonnegative for $x\geq 0$, but a general proof remains open.

370017.title: Polynomial-time hardness conjecture for balanced independent sets in dense random bipartite graphs
370017.statement: Let $G_{\mathrm{bip}}(n,p)$ be the random bipartite graph in the online model considered in the source, let $\gamma$ be the balance parameter, and let $\alpha_{\rm COMP}$ denote the computational threshold defined earlier in the paper. **Polynomial-time hardness conjecture.** For any $\epsilon>0$ and $p=\Theta(1)$, no polynomial-time algorithm finds a $\gamma$-balanced independent set of size $(1+\epsilon)\alpha_{\rm COMP}$ in $G_{\mathrm{bip}}(n,p)$ whp. This conjecture concerns the computational gap for online balanced independent sets in dense random bipartite graphs; the paper's results provide rigorous evidence for the claimed threshold, while the conjecture itself remains open.
